doc.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Finding a record label: Alliance bankruptcy and small labels
summary: He explains how distribution changed, how the Alliance collapse hurt independent labels, and how too much product floods stores.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: What’s it like trying to find — I guess we’ve probably already answered this question — but trying to find a record label these days?

These days it’s more difficult than before I think. It’s unfortunate but I would say the reason, there has been some not so good things that have happened to the record industry. A couple of years ago I think the Alliance, which was a large distribution, independent distributor — the nature of the record business has changed so that, and the way, back when Columbia, it was Columbia before it was Sony and Warner Brothers, they had in- house public relations departments and how everything was kind of in-house. The distribution was their distribution, they had huge distribution. And later the age of the specialists came on and they started to farm things out to — you know the PR became, as opposed to them trying to house everything so that happened. Alliance Distribution was one of them. They had sort of bought up all these small distributions so they had this major network of distribution throughout the country. And they went bankrupt a couple of years ago, two or three years ago. And that sent a ripple effect through the distribution network and a lot of distribution labels — I mean small labels, independent labels, which were great, it was a great thing, and during the time when I was coming here. Like India Navigation. That was the Contemporary. These great labels that had really good music and recorded some great people. You know I mean, with Contemporary, that was one of

the first labels Sonny Rollins recorded for. And Ornette Coleman recorded on that label you know. Those kinds of labels, it’s now more difficult for them to exist. But those labels made it possible for artists to be artists and get names and do things, whereas the major labels, the big ones, you were much more restricted in what you could do, what they wanted you to do and what they would do for you. So because of that bankruptcy going with Alliance, a lot of the smaller labels couldn’t survive. So a lot of them have disappeared, those labels, that were really good, I think they were very good for the music. So now this is the thing that we’re dealing with. There’s some independent labels coming up. A lot of musicians are doing their own labels these days.
Right. There’s an awful lot of product out there.
There’s a lot of product out there. And that’s another thing. I mean you can do a record, you can.

That’s again, you could but should you. And you know the stores are inundated with product that nobody knows who these people are so it’s difficult for people to go in there and look in a bin and see hundreds and hundreds and hundreds of CDs in there and they don’t know what to buy. There’s not a lot of radio these days. So it’s not an easy situation. It’s just very difficult. Thing have to change. I mean things always change, it’s just a matter of being able to make it through the change.
I hope that answers your question.
